banner: A technical assessment prepared for counsel. It states what the documents show and how each AI use is classified. It gives no legal advice and recommends no product.

boundaries.name: {Entity} to third party
boundaries.parties: The {entity} and a material service provider: claims manager, underwriting agency or broker acting under delegated authority

boundaries.name: Third party to fourth party
boundaries.parties: The provider and the platform behind it: the technology, pricing or AI model the provider relies on

boundaries.name: {Entity}'s own use
boundaries.parties: The {entity}'s legal, claims and compliance staff and an external AI service

criteria: The {entity} is itself asked for evidence

interviews.who: Head of AI or AI governance
interviews.purpose: Agree the approach. Walk through the inventory and its known limits

interviews.who: Owner of each arrangement in the set
interviews.purpose: What the provider does, where AI is known or suspected, what has been asked of the provider
How agreements are renewed and what evidence terms exist today
Critical operations, tolerances and how provider risk is monitored now

interviews.who: Users of each external AI service at B3
interviews.purpose: What the service is used for and what it is permitted to do

fields.name: Arrangement ID
fields.format: ARR-01 onward, from the set register

fields.name: Where the AI acts
fields.format: Own staff · provider · platform behind a provider

fields.name: Business function and critical operation supported
fields.format: Free text, plus the critical operation name from the {entity}'s CPS 230 list, or "none"

fields.name: Platform and model provider behind it
Location of each party, and any offshoring
What the AI does
fields.format: Two sentences, plain words, verbs only from the source

fields.name: Human involvement
fields.format: A person acts · a person decides · the output is the decision · unattended

fields.name: Credentials and systems the AI can change
Agreement terms on information, audit, sub-contracting and notification
Evidence the system could produce
fields.format: Description of the record and where it would be generated

fields.name: Rights the {entity} holds
fields.format: Passive · significant influence · contractual · control or board seat

fields.name: Required rung and grading
fields.format: E0 to E6, graded requirement · expectation · better view

fields.name: Finding and gap owner
fields.format: F1 to F4 (section 9.1), with named owner

questions7.q: Does a separate CPS 230 nexus exist? Is the party within the {entity}'s group (para 5)?
questions7.facts: Legal entity and ownership of each party

questions7.q: Is there a separate relationship that may engage CPS 230: a service to the {entity}, or part of a chain supporting one (para 54)?
questions7.facts: The service provided, the critical operation it supports, and each link in the chain

questions7.q: What rights does the {entity} or its manager hold?
questions7.scale: Passive · significant influence · contractual, including binder and claims agreements · control or board seat
questions7.facts: Verbatim information, audit, sub-contracting and notification terms

questions7.q: Where is each party, and does location change what can be obtained? Enforceability, data access and audit rights; offshoring (paras 53(b) and 60(b))
questions7.scale: Per party: no effect · limits evidence · prevents evidence
questions7.facts: Country of each party and of where the AI runs

questions7.q: What authority has been delegated to the AI, and what can its action produce?
questions7.scale: Productivity · analytical · decision · transactional · agentic · actuating
questions7.by: Triodian classifies; counsel determines the authority delegated

questions7.scale: Immaterial · contract breach · financial loss · {customer} harm · critical-operation disruption
questions7.facts: Critical operation link, tolerance, incident history

questions7.q: What evidence can reasonably be required?
questions7.scale: None · disclosure · attestation · event notification · audit · continuous telemetry · deterministic actuation control
questions7.facts: Indicative rung, evidence received, evidence producible, checkability

authorityTests: Does a person act on the output, or does the output take effect without one?
Does the output move money, change a policy or claim record, or commit the {entity}?
Does the AI hold credentials to act across steps or systems without a person starting each step?
Does field 13 show that the AI can write to a system of record using its own credentials?

tiers.name: Productivity
tiers.def: Drafts, summarises, searches. A person still acts
tiers.test: A person writes or sends the final output

tiers.name: Analytical
tiers.def: Scores, ranks, recommends. A person decides
tiers.test: The output is an input to a named person's decision

tiers.name: Decision
tiers.def: Approves, declines, triages. The output is the decision; no person reviews before it takes effect
tiers.test: No person reviews before the outcome takes effect

tiers.name: Transactional
tiers.def: Prices, allocates, pays. Money or positions move
tiers.test: The output commits or moves money

tiers.name: Agentic
tiers.def: Plans and acts across steps and tools, unattended
tiers.test: The AI starts its own next step

tiers.name: Actuation
tiers.def: Holds credentials that change systems, assets or infrastructure
tiers.test: The AI can write to systems of record under its own credentials

consequences.name: Immaterial
consequences.def: No effect outside the team using it

consequences.name: Contract breach
consequences.def: The provider or {entity} would be in breach of an agreement term

consequences.name: Financial loss
consequences.def: Loss to the {entity} above its reporting threshold for the operation

consequences.name: {Customer} harm
consequences.def: {ACustomer} is wrongly declined, delayed, charged or paid

consequences.name: Critical-operation disruption
consequences.def: A critical operation moves outside the tolerance the board has set

rungs.name: Disclosure
rungs.def: A statement of what AI is used, where and for what.

rungs.name: Attestation
rungs.def: A signed statement that the AI operated within stated limits over a period.

rungs.name: Event notification
rungs.def: Notice when a defined trigger is crossed. Also called trigger reporting.

rungs.name: Audit
rungs.def: A right to examine the aggregate record, exercised by the {entity} or its verifier.

rungs.name: Continuous telemetry
rungs.def: A stream of aggregate measures against the declared appetite. Also called continuous evidence.

rungs.name: Deterministic actuation control
rungs.def: A control at the point of action, independent of the AI's reasoning, with a signed record of what was requested, what applied and what was allowed.

tests.name: Produced
tests.q: Does a record of this type exist, or could the system generate it without redesign?

tests.name: Aggregate
tests.q: Can it be given without individual decisions, {customer} data or the model?

tests.name: Reachable
tests.q: Is there a route for it to reach the {entity}: a term in force, or a contracting point where one could be added?

tests.name: Checkable
tests.q: Can someone independent of the party producing it verify it?

tests.name: Timely
tests.q: Can it arrive in time for the {entity} to act and meet its own notification obligations?

findings.name: Evidence obtainable
findings.cond: Obtainable rung is at or above the required rung

findings.name: Gap
findings.cond: Obtainable rung is below the required rung

findings.name: No reasonable reach
findings.cond: Counsel determines the {entity} cannot reasonably require evidence at this boundary

findings.name: Not determinable on documents
findings.cond: The documents do not show whether AI is used, or what it can do

T1: The provider, or the {entity}’s AI team at B3
A boundary control and evidence design, if the {entity} asks
T2: Redesign of the record so it carries aggregates and references only
T3: Evidence terms at the next contracting point, with a technical schedule beside the clauses
T5: Notification timing aligned to the {entity}'s own windows

reviews.name: Set review
reviews.tests: Selection criteria applied; each boundary type represented

reviews.name: Register completeness
reviews.tests: Fields 1 to 14 complete or not known; every value sourced and dated

reviews.name: Classification review
reviews.reviewer: A second Triodian reviewer, not the classifier
reviews.tests: Tier re-derived from fields 11 to 13 without sight of the original; differences resolved and logged

reviews.name: Validation
reviews.tests: Rules in sections 8.3 and 8.4 applied consistently across entries; every adjustment has a reason; every obtainable rung has five test results

reviews.name: Legal-line check
reviews.tests: No sentence states what the law requires; "required" and "gap" used only as section 10.4 allows

reviews.name: Counsel review
reviews.tests: Draft seen by counsel first; determinations transcribed accurately

reviews.name: Independent check
reviews.tests: Is the assessment sound, and are its findings supported?

annexOutline: Purpose, and the question the assessment answers
What was and was not done: no data, no provider involvement, no production access, no legal advice
The set, and why each arrangement was selected
Method: register, seven questions, ladder, obtainability test
Patterns across the set: which test fails most often, and at which boundary
Routes available for each gap, without recommendation of any product
Limitations and confidence, including the not-known count
Appendices: register extract, question log, source index

arrangement.def: One relationship that is assessed: a provider, the platform behind a provider, or an external AI service used by the {entity}’s staff

set.def: The arrangements chosen for assessment against six criteria and agreed by the GC

entry.def: One place where AI acts within an arrangement, recorded in 26 fields

boundary.def: A point where evidence must pass between two parties: B1, between the {entity} and a provider; B2, between a provider and the platform behind it; B3, the {entity}’s own use of an external AI service

seven.def: The seven questions asked of every arrangement, in a fixed order, from nexus to evidence

nexus.def: Whether a party falls within the {entity}’s group for CPS 230 purposes. Counsel determines this

rights.def: What the {entity} can require of a party: passive, significant influence, contractual, or control or board seat. Counsel determines this

source.def: The document and page, or the interview and date, that a value comes from

expected.def: The evidence the board expects for this authority tier and consequence level, taken from the [[calibration|calibration set]] (P3)

indicative.def: The evidence rung the framework sets by default when no calibration set is loaded

required.def: The evidence the {entity} can reasonably require at this boundary, as determined with [[counsel]]

obtainable.def: The highest evidence rung that passes all five [[obtest|obtainability tests]]

obtest.def: Five conditions, T1 to T5, that evidence must meet to be obtainable: produced, aggregate, reachable, checkable and timely

T1.def: A record of this type exists, or could be generated without redesign

T2.def: The record can be given without individual decisions, {customer} data or the model

T3.def: There is a term in force, or a contracting point, by which the record can reach the {entity}

T4.def: Someone independent of the party that produces the record can verify it

T5.def: It can arrive in time for the {entity} to act and meet its own notification obligations

F1.def: The obtainable rung meets the required rung

F2.def: The obtainable rung falls short of the required rung

F3.def: Counsel has determined that the {entity} cannot reasonably require evidence here. This is a conclusion, not a gap

F4.def: The documents cannot show whether, or how, AI is used

blind.def: Review point R3 (classification review). A second person sets the tier from the facts alone (fields 11 to 13), without seeing the first classification

peer.def: The Triodian person who sets the tier a second time, [[blind|without seeing the first classification]]. Never the person who classified the entry

ir.def: The party outside Triodian that checks whether the assessment is sound and its findings supported, on behalf of the CRO

qc.def: A numbered written question that asks counsel for a legal determination. It is never answered in a working paper

transcribed.def: Counsel’s written response, entered word for word by a Triodian person, with the question reference

schedule.def: The evidence items, tolerance levels and triggers, written to sit beside the flow-down clauses counsel drafts (DL4)

annex.def: Triodian’s report of the assessment, issued in Triodian’s own name (DL5)

handback.def: The AI uses found that are not on the {entity}’s inventory, handed back to the inventory owner (DL6)

legalline.def: Review point R5. A scan of draft outputs for wording that states what the law requires, so that it can be removed or reworded

diff.def: A record of what changed in the results when a new version of the calibration set was loaded

privilege.def: The marking that counsel directs for the work. It is printed on every output

tier.def: How much the AI can do on its own, from A1 (productivity) to A6 (actuation)

consequence.def: How serious a failure would be, from C1 (immaterial) to C5 (critical-operation disruption)

rung.def: A level of evidence on the evidence ladder, from E0 (none) to E6 (deterministic actuation control)

calibration.def: The eleven parameters, P1 to P11, that the board sets through the AI Risk Appetite app. They set the {entity}’s expectations, limits and priorities in this app

ceiling.def: The highest [[tier|authority tier]] the board accepts for AI in a given function and location (P1)

aboveCeiling.def: An AI use whose authority tier is higher than the [[ceiling]]. It is reported beside the finding, never as part of it

confidence.def: How firmly an obtainable rung is established: high if the record has been seen, medium if a document describes it, low if it is inferred

notKnown.def: A fact the documents do not show. It is counted and reported, never estimated

counsel.def: The law firm leading the engagement. Every legal determination is the {entity}’s and its counsel’s

separation.def: The person who classifies an entry and its peer reviewer must be different people. The validation person (R4) must not have classified or reviewed any entry in the set. The person who signs the annex must not be the only peer reviewer of any entry

concentration.def: The share of critical operations in the set that depend on a single platform or model provider, measured against the board’s limit (P9). Each critical operation is counted once. Each unknown platform is listed separately, never grouped with other unknowns

roleLimits.def: Who can do what. Set-up and the people list: the method owner or the delivery manager (administrators can also change set-up). Agreeing the set (R1): the GC and counsel, each recording their own agreement. Facts and classification: an assessor or the method owner, but never the peer reviewer of that entry. Blind re-derivation (R3): a peer reviewer who did not classify the entry. Validation (R4): a validation person who has not classified or reviewed any entry. Legal-line check (R5): the method owner. Counsel review (R6): counsel. Review points: the independent reviewer logs and closes them, and Triodian responds. Independent check (R7): the independent reviewer, when reporting through counsel, or the CRO, when the independent reviewer reports directly to the CRO. Fields 23 to 25: counsel, or Triodian by transcribing counsel’s written response. Annex: the method owner, as long as they are not the only peer reviewer of any entry

frameworkMarkdown:
# AI Use Assessment Framework

11 October 2026 · Updated for the changes in the build specification, section 0.2

## 1. Summary

The AI use assessment establishes, for a representative set of {anEntity}'s arrangements, where AI acts, what it is able to do, and what evidence of its behaviour can be produced at each boundary in the chain. It is the technical half of a joint engagement led by counsel. Counsel answers what the {entity} can require; this assessment answers what can actually be produced.

| Item | Position |
| --- | --- |
| Question answered | At each boundary in the chain, what evidence of AI behaviour can be produced, measured against the board's appetite? |
| Unit of assessment | One arrangement: a material service provider, the platform behind it, or an external AI service the {entity}'s own staff use |
| Instruments | The AI use register, the seven questions and the evidence ladder |
| Duration | Three to four weeks |
| Inputs | The {entity}'s AI inventory and the agreement for each arrangement in scope |
| Not required | {Customer} data, provider involvement, production access |
| Outputs | The register, one finding per arrangement, a technical schedule and a technical annex in Triodian's name |
| Independent check | The independent reviewer, on behalf of the CRO |
| Measure | {regulator}'s standards and expectations. The assessment is solution-agnostic and presents no product |

**Status of this document.** The method, the seven questions, the ladder, the roles and the outputs come from counsel's planning deck (October 2026) and the AI Counsel Briefing (12 September 2026). The field-level detail, codes, rating rules, weekly plan and templates are drafted here to make the method executable. Section 12 lists each drafted element that needs confirmation.

**Standing rule.** Every legal determination is the {entity}'s and its counsel's. Triodian supplies the framework, the facts and the technical classification. Nothing in the assessment or its working papers states a legal conclusion.

## 2. Scope and boundaries

### 2.1 The chain and its boundaries

The assessment follows one chain and tests three kinds of boundary. Each register entry and each finding is tagged with one of them.

| Code | Boundary | Parties | What passes across it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | {Entity} to third party | The {entity} and a material service provider: claims manager, underwriting agency or broker acting under delegated authority | Agreement terms outward; aggregate evidence back |
| B2 | Third party to fourth party | The provider and the platform behind it: the technology, pricing or AI model the provider relies on | Flow-down terms outward; what the provider can obtain back |
| B3 | {Entity}'s own use | The {entity}'s legal, claims and compliance staff and an external AI service | The {entity}'s own rules outward; a signed record back |

### 2.2 The representative set

The assessment covers a representative set of arrangements agreed with the General Counsel, not the whole estate. The default is four arrangements, the number used in the September counsel briefing.

Selection criteria, applied in this order:

1. **A live trigger.** A regulator request, a remediation or a major provider renewal that sets a date.
2. **AI inside a provider.** Business written through agencies or outside claims managers, where the agreement holds the audit rights.
3. **The {entity} is itself asked for evidence.** For example a group life {entity} answering to superannuation trustees.
4. **Coverage of boundary types.** At least one B1, one B2 reached through it, and one B3.
5. **Spread of authority.** At least one arrangement where AI decides or transacts, and one where it only assists.
6. **Likely above the authority ceiling.** An arrangement where AI is likely to hold more authority than the board's ceiling for the function (P1). Applies only when a calibration set is loaded.

### 2.3 In scope

- AI used in or supporting a service to the {entity}, wherever in the chain it sits.
- AI used by the {entity}'s own staff through an external service.
- The agreement, and any schedule or side letter, for each arrangement in the set.
- The {entity}'s existing AI inventory, AI governance framework and material service provider register.

### 2.4 Out of scope

- **Legal advice.** Reach, applicability, grading and privilege are counsel's.
- **{Customer} or claims data.** The assessment works from documents and interviews.
- **Provider involvement.** No provider is approached. Obtainability is assessed from the {entity}'s side.
- **Production access.** No system is connected to, tested or monitored.
- **Model testing.** No model is evaluated for accuracy, bias or drift.
- **Products and gap filling.** Closing a gap is a separate decision for the {entity} after the findings.
- **The whole estate.** Arrangements outside the set are not assessed. Uses found outside the inventory are handed to its owner.

## 3. Framework at a glance

Three instruments are applied in four steps, the same way to every arrangement at every client.

### 3.1 The three instruments

| Instrument | What it is | Section |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AI use register | One entry for each place AI acts in the chain, with a fixed set of fields | 6 |
| The seven questions | The ordered questions put to every arrangement. Two sit under all of them: what can the {entity} require, and what can actually be produced | 7 |
| Evidence ladder | A scale of evidence types, matched to what the AI can do | 8 |

### 3.2 The four steps

1. **Confirm the set.** A representative set of arrangements, agreed with the GC.
2. **Map the AI.** Where AI acts, what authority it holds and who stands behind it. Each use becomes a register entry.
3. **Classify and test.** The consequence of each use, and the evidence obtainable at each boundary.
4. **Questions to counsel.** Legal questions go to counsel in writing. Counsel sees every draft first. Counsel's determinations are then recorded against each entry and the finding is set.

### 3.3 The logic of a finding

Each arrangement produces three positions on the ladder. The finding is the relationship between the last two.

| Position | Meaning | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Indicative rung | The evidence type that corresponds to what the AI can do | Triodian, by rule (section 8) |
| Required rung | The evidence the {entity} can reasonably require, given reach and rights | The {entity} and counsel |
| Obtainable rung | The highest evidence type that can in fact be produced and independently checked | Triodian, by test (section 8.4) |

### 3.4 Operating principles

- **Aggregate only.** No individual decisions, no {customer} data, no access to a provider's model.
- **Start from what exists.** The {entity}'s own inventory is the first input. Gaps go back to its owner to fix.
- **"No reasonable reach" is a conclusion.** It is documented as a finding, not treated as a gap.
- **Solution-agnostic.** The test is {regulator}'s: can the evidence be produced, and can someone independent check it?
- **Every stage can stop.** The assessment leaves a usable register and findings whether or not anything follows.

## 4. Roles and governance

### 4.1 Parties

| Party | Role | Engaged by | Where it stops |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The {entity} | Client. The CRO raises the risk; the GC decides the brief and owns the outcome | n/a | n/a |
| Counsel | Leads the engagement, holds the client, engages both firms, owns every legal call | The {entity} | n/a |
| Triodian | Technical party. Does the assessment and the register. Responsible for the result | Counsel | Gives no legal advice. Fills gaps only if the {entity} asks, as a separate decision |
| Independent reviewer | Independent check of Triodian's assessment, on behalf of the CRO | Counsel or the CRO, separately from Triodian (to be confirmed) | Does not do the assessment or build any control. Gives no legal advice |

### 4.2 Responsibility by activity

R = does the work. A = accountable for it. C = consulted. I = informed.

| Activity | GC | {Entity} AI and risk teams | Counsel | Triodian | Independent reviewer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Decide the brief and the set | A | C | R | C | I |
| Brief the AI, governance and safety teams | I | C | A | R | I |
| Supply inventory and agreements | A | R | C | I | I |
| Build and extend the register | I | C | I | A, R | I |
| Classify authority and failure consequence | I | C | C | A, R | I |
| Test evidence obtainability | I | C | C | A, R | I |
| Determine nexus, rights, reach and required evidence | A | I | R | C | I |
| Grade requirement, expectation or better view | A | I | R | I | I |
| Draft findings and technical annex | I | C | C | A, R | I |
| Check the assessment and its findings | I | I | A | C | R |
| Board paper and flow-down clause schedule | A | I | R | C | I |

### 4.3 Team

| Role | Responsibility in the assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Method owner | Scope, sequence and the evidence each stage has to produce. Signs the technical annex |
| Delivery manager | Plan, document requests, interview schedule, issue log |
| AI architect | Technical reading of each system: authority, credentials, where a record could be produced |
| Validation | Checks the measures without having written them, before anything goes to the independent reviewer |

### 4.4 Rules of engagement

- **Counsel first.** Every draft goes to counsel before anyone at the {entity} sees it.
- **Legal questions in writing.** Any point needing a legal view is logged as a numbered question to counsel (template in section 9.5) and is not answered in a working paper.
- **Privilege.** The work is scoped through counsel, on the privilege position counsel determines. Document marking, storage and circulation follow counsel's instruction.
- **One technical party.** Counsel deals with Triodian for all technical matters.
- **Independence of the check.** The independent reviewer receives the register, worksheets and annex from counsel or the CRO, not from Triodian, and reports on behalf of the CRO.

## 5. Workplan

The plan below fits the four steps into four weeks. Where the set is small and documents arrive on day one, weeks 2 and 3 compress into one.

### 5.1 Phases

| Phase | When | Activities | Output | Exit gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0. Mobilise | Before week 1 | Counsel convenes the legal and technical briefing. GC decides the brief. Privilege position and document handling set by counsel. Document request issued | Signed brief. Document request list. Agreed contacts | GC has confirmed the brief in writing |
| 1. Confirm the set | Week 1, days 1 to 2 | Apply the selection criteria in section 2.2. Agree the arrangements and their boundary types with the GC | Set register: arrangement ID, parties, boundary type, reason selected | GC and counsel agree the set |
| 2. Map the AI | Week 1, day 3, to end of week 2 | Brief the AI, governance and safety teams. Take the {entity}'s inventory as the first input. Read each agreement. Interview arrangement owners. Extend the register down the chain | Register with fields 1 to 14 complete (section 6). Interview notes. Source index | Every entry has a source and a date. Uses not on the inventory are logged for hand-back |
| 3. Classify and test | Weeks 2 to 3 | Classify authority and failure consequence. Set the indicative rung. Run the obtainability test at each boundary. Internal validation review | Register fields 15 to 22 complete. Classification rationale per entry. Draft worksheets | Validation review passed with no open exceptions |
| 4. Questions to counsel | Week 3 | Issue the numbered question set to counsel. Record counsel's determinations on nexus, rights, location and required evidence | Question log with responses. Register fields 23 to 25 complete | Every question answered, or recorded as open with an owner |
| 5. Findings and report | Weeks 3 to 4 | Set one finding per arrangement. Draft the technical schedule and annex. Draft to counsel first | Finding worksheets. Technical schedule. Technical annex, draft | Counsel accepts the draft for independent check |
| 6. Independent check | Week 4 | The pack goes to the independent reviewer through the agreed reporting line. Triodian answers its queries through the same line. Corrections made and logged | The independent reviewer's check, reported on behalf of the CRO. Final annex | The check is confirmed complete through the agreed reporting line |
| 7. Close | End of week 4 | Hand uses not on the inventory back to its owner. Hand the register to counsel. Archive working papers as counsel directs | Hand-back list. Final register. Closure note | GC receives counsel's advice with the annex attached |

### 5.2 Document request list

Issued in phase 0 through counsel.

| Ref | Document | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Current AI inventory or register, with owner and date | First input to the register |
| D2 | AI governance framework and acceptable-use policy | Authority and the {entity}'s own rules at B3 |
| D3 | Material service provider register | Confirming the set and boundary types |
| D4 | Board risk appetite statement and tolerance levels for the critical operations in the set | The appetite the evidence is measured against |
| D5 | The agreement for each arrangement, with schedules, service descriptions and side letters | Rights, audit and information terms, sub-contracting terms |
| D6 | Delegated authority schedules for each binder or claims agreement | What authority the provider holds, and so what its AI can hold |
| D7 | Any provider disclosure about AI use already received: due diligence responses, attestations, notices | Evidence already obtainable |
| D8 | Licence terms and security documentation for each external AI service staff use | B3 entries |
| D9 | Existing assurance over the arrangements: audit reports, control reports, certifications | What existing assurance already covers |
| D10 | Incident and near-miss records involving AI in the set, last 24 months | Failure consequence |

### 5.3 Interviews

| Who | Purpose | Length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Head of AI or AI governance | Agree the approach. Walk through the inventory and its known limits | 60 min |
| Owner of each arrangement in the set | What the provider does, where AI is known or suspected, what has been asked of the provider | 45 min each |
| Procurement or vendor management | How agreements are renewed and what evidence terms exist today | 45 min |
| Operational risk, second line | Critical operations, tolerances and how provider risk is monitored now | 45 min |
| Users of each external AI service at B3 | What the service is used for and what it is permitted to do | 30 min each |

## 6. AI use register

The register holds one entry for each place AI acts within an arrangement. An arrangement with AI at the provider and at the platform behind it has at least two entries.

### 6.1 How it is built

1. **Brief the AI teams first.** Agree the approach with the AI, governance and safety teams.
2. **Start from what exists.** The {entity}'s own AI inventory is the first input.
3. **Extend it down the chain.** Add the AI inside providers and the platforms behind them.
4. **Classify each entry.** Authority, consequence, rights and evidence.
5. **Hand the gaps back.** Uses not on the inventory go to its owner to add.

### 6.2 Fields

The deck names eight things each entry records. The 26 fields below break those eight into items a reviewer can test one at a time.

| # | Field | Allowed values or format | Completed by | Phase |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Entry ID | REG-001 onward | Triodian | 2 |
| 2 | Arrangement ID | ARR-01 onward, from the set register | Triodian | 2 |
| 3 | Boundary type | B1, B2, B3 | Triodian | 2 |
| 4 | Where the AI acts | Own staff · provider · platform behind a provider | Triodian | 2 |
| 5 | Business function and critical operation supported | Free text, plus the critical operation name from the {entity}'s CPS 230 list, or "none" | Triodian with arrangement owner | 2 |
| 6 | On the {entity}'s inventory | Yes · no · partly | Triodian | 2 |
| 7 | System name and purpose | Free text | Triodian | 2 |
| 8 | Supplier | Legal entity name | Triodian | 2 |
| 9 | Platform and model provider behind it | Legal entity names, or "not known" | Triodian | 2 |
| 10 | Location of each party, and any offshoring | Country per party | Triodian | 2 |
| 11 | What the AI does | Two sentences, plain words, verbs only from the source | Triodian | 2 |
| 12 | Human involvement | A person acts · a person decides · the output is the decision · unattended | Triodian | 2 |
| 13 | Credentials and systems the AI can change | List, or "none" | Triodian | 2 |
| 14 | Agreement terms on information, audit, sub-contracting and notification | Clause references with verbatim extracts | Triodian | 2 |
| 15 | Authority tier | A1 to A6 (section 8.1) | Triodian | 3 |
| 16 | Failure consequence | C1 to C5 (section 8.2) | Triodian | 3 |
| 17 | Indicative rung | E0 to E6 (section 8.3) | Triodian, by rule | 3 |
| 18 | Evidence currently received | Rung and description, or "none" | Triodian | 3 |
| 19 | Evidence the system could produce | Description of the record and where it would be generated | Triodian | 3 |
| 20 | Independently checkable | Yes · no · partly, with reason | Triodian | 3 |
| 21 | Obtainable rung | E0 to E6 (section 8.4) | Triodian, by test | 3 |
| 22 | Confidence in obtainability | High · medium · low | Triodian | 3 |
| 23 | Nexus, relationship and location determination | Counsel's wording, with question reference | Counsel | 4 |
| 24 | Rights the {entity} holds | Passive · significant influence · contractual · control or board seat | Counsel | 4 |
| 25 | Required rung and grading | E0 to E6, graded requirement · expectation · better view | Counsel | 4 |
| 26 | Finding and gap owner | F1 to F4 (section 9.1), with named owner | Triodian, after counsel | 5 |

**Calibration flags.** With a calibration set loaded, each entry also carries an above-ceiling flag (P1) and a location marking (P8) for where the provider is established and where the AI runs. Flags are reported beside the finding, never as part of it.

### 6.3 Completion rules

- **Every value has a source.** Each field carries a source reference (document and page, or interview and date). A value without a source is recorded as "not known", never estimated.
- **Field 11 is descriptive, field 15 is the judgement.** The description is written before the tier is chosen, so a reviewer can re-derive the tier from it.
- **Fields 23 to 25 are never completed by Triodian.** They are transcribed from counsel's written response, with the question number.
- **"Not known" is a valid entry and is counted.** The annex reports how many fields are not known, by arrangement.
- **Confidence (field 22) is low by default at B2.** No provider is approached, so a fourth-party rung rests on documents alone unless field 14 or D7 supports it.
- **One classifier, one reviewer.** Fields 15 to 22 record who classified and who reviewed. They cannot be the same person.

## 7. The seven questions

The questions are worked in order for every arrangement. The determination at each step is the {entity}'s and its counsel's. Triodian supplies the framework and the facts each determination needs.

The paragraph references are those cited in the two decks. Counsel confirms them against the current instrument before they appear in any deliverable.

### 7.1 Question set

| # | Question | Answer scale | Determined by | Facts Triodian supplies | Register fields |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Does a separate CPS 230 nexus exist? Is the party within the {entity}'s group (para 5)? | Yes · no | Counsel | Legal entity and ownership of each party | 8, 9, 23 |
| 2 | Is there a separate relationship that may engage CPS 230: a service to the {entity}, or part of a chain supporting one (para 54)? | Yes · no | Counsel | The service provided, the critical operation it supports, and each link in the chain | 5, 8, 9, 23 |
| 3 | What rights does the {entity} or its manager hold? | Passive · significant influence · contractual, including binder and claims agreements · control or board seat | Counsel | Verbatim information, audit, sub-contracting and notification terms | 14, 24 |
| 4 | Where is each party, and does location change what can be obtained? Enforceability, data access and audit rights; offshoring (paras 53(b) and 60(b)) | Per party: no effect · limits evidence · prevents evidence | Counsel | Country of each party and of where the AI runs | 10, 23 |
| 5 | What authority has been delegated to the AI, and what can its action produce? | Productivity · analytical · decision · transactional · agentic · actuating | Triodian classifies; counsel determines the authority delegated | Function, human involvement, credentials | 11, 12, 13, 15 |
| 6 | What could failure do? | Immaterial · contract breach · financial loss · {customer} harm · critical-operation disruption | Triodian classifies; {entity} confirms | Critical operation link, tolerance, incident history | 5, 16 |
| 7 | What evidence can reasonably be required? | None · disclosure · attestation · event notification · audit · continuous telemetry · deterministic actuation control | Counsel determines; Triodian tests obtainability | Indicative rung, evidence received, evidence producible, checkability | 17 to 22, 25 |

### 7.2 Tests under each question

**Q1 and Q2, nexus and relationship.** Triodian does not answer these. It supplies an entity and service map for each arrangement: who contracts with whom, which entity operates the AI, and which critical operation the service supports. Two points from {regulator}'s guidance, as cited in the counsel briefing, are flagged for counsel on each arrangement: a related party providing a service is assessed on the same footing as a third party, and providers relied on for the same critical operation may be assessed as a cohort.

**Q3, rights.** For each agreement Triodian extracts, without interpretation:

- any term giving the {entity} information about how the service is performed
- any audit or access right, and what it reaches
- any term on sub-contractors and whether the {entity} must be notified or consent
- any incident or event notification term and its timing
- any term that mentions AI, automation, models or automated decision-making
- the next contracting point: renewal, amendment or review date

**Q4, location.** Triodian records where each party is incorporated, where the service is performed and where the AI runs. Where any of these is not known from the documents, the entry says so.

**Q5, authority.** Three tests, each answered from the source documents:

1. Does a person act on the output, or does the output take effect without one?
2. Does the output move money, change a policy or claim record, or commit the {entity}?
3. Does the AI hold credentials to act across steps or systems without a person starting each step?

The tier follows from the answers (section 8.1). Whether that authority was validly delegated under the agreement is counsel's question.

**Q6, failure.** The classification takes the most serious credible outcome if the AI acted wrongly and went undetected for one reporting period. It is anchored to the {entity}'s own tolerance for the critical operation in field 5 where one exists.

**Q7, evidence.** Split into its two halves and kept separate throughout:

- **What can be required** is counsel's determination and becomes the required rung.
- **What can be produced** is Triodian's test (section 8.4) and becomes the obtainable rung.

### 7.3 Stop rules

- **Q1 to Q3 all negative.** If counsel finds no nexus, no relationship and only passive rights, the arrangement is recorded as F3, no reasonable reach. Q5 and Q6 are still classified so the conclusion is documented against what the AI can do.
- **Q5 at productivity with Q6 immaterial.** Disclosure is the most the ladder indicates. The obtainability test is limited to whether disclosure exists.
- **Facts unavailable.** Where the documents do not show whether AI is used at a provider or platform, the entry is recorded as F4, not determinable on documents, with the specific question that would resolve it.

## 8. Classification and the evidence ladder

### 8.1 Authority tiers (question 5)

Tier definitions are from the counsel briefing. The insurance examples are illustrative and are replaced with the client's own in each engagement.

| Code | Tier | Definition | Deciding test | Illustrative insurance example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | Productivity | Drafts, summarises, searches. A person still acts | A person writes or sends the final output | A claims handler uses a copilot to summarise a file |
| A2 | Analytical | Scores, ranks, recommends. A person decides | The output is an input to a named person's decision | A fraud score shown to an assessor |
| A3 | Decision | Approves, declines, triages. The output is the decision | No person reviews before the outcome takes effect | Automatic triage of a claim to fast-track or investigation |
| A4 | Transactional | Prices, allocates, pays. Money or positions move | The output commits or moves money | Automated pricing under a binder, or straight-through claim payment |
| A5 | Agentic | Plans and acts across steps and tools, unattended | The AI starts its own next step | An agent that gathers documents, contacts a repairer and books an assessment |
| A6 | Actuation | Holds credentials that change systems, assets or infrastructure | The AI can write to systems of record under its own credentials | An agent with write access to the policy administration system |

Where a system fits two tiers, the higher one is recorded and the reason noted.

### 8.2 Failure consequence (question 6)

| Code | Consequence | Meaning for the assessment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Immaterial | No effect outside the team using it |
| C2 | Contract breach | The provider or {entity} would be in breach of an agreement term |
| C3 | Financial loss | Loss to the {entity} above its reporting threshold for the operation |
| C4 | {Customer} harm | {ACustomer} is wrongly declined, delayed, charged or paid |
| C5 | Critical-operation disruption | A critical operation moves outside the tolerance the board has set |

### 8.3 The evidence ladder (question 7)

The two decks use slightly different names for three rungs. Both are shown; the first is used in this document.

| Code | Rung | Also called | What the {entity} holds | Produced by | Frequency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E0 | None |  | Nothing | n/a | n/a |
| E1 | Disclosure |  | A statement of what AI is used, where and for what | The provider | On change, or annually |
| E2 | Attestation |  | A signed statement that the AI operated within stated limits over a period | The provider | Per reporting period |
| E3 | Event notification | Trigger reporting | Notice when a defined trigger is crossed | The provider | On event, within an agreed time |
| E4 | Audit |  | A right to examine the aggregate record, exercised by the {entity} or its verifier | The {entity} or an independent party | On demand or scheduled |
| E5 | Continuous telemetry | Continuous evidence | A stream of aggregate measures against the declared appetite | The system | Each window |
| E6 | Deterministic actuation control | Deterministic control | A control at the point of action, independent of the AI's reasoning, with a signed record of what was requested, what applied and what was allowed | The system | Each action, reported in aggregate |

**Indicative rung.** The base rule pairs each authority tier with one rung.

| Authority tier | A1 | A2 | A3 | A4 | A5 | A6 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Indicative rung | E1 | E2 | E3 | E4 | E5 | E6 |

**Adjustment for failure consequence (proposed, for confirmation).** The decks set the base rule only. This document proposes two adjustments so that question 6 affects the result:

- C1 with A1 or A2: the indicative rung drops by one.
- C4 or C5 with A1 to A4: the indicative rung rises by one.

Every adjustment is recorded with its reason. The indicative rung is a technical starting point. Which rung applies is a determination for the {entity}.

**Expected rung.** Where the board has set its appetite under the AI Risk Appetite Framework, the calibration set's expectation (P3) replaces the indicative rung, and the obtainability test starts there. The board sets that expectation in decision 3, starting from the evidence the {entity} holds today, not from the table above. Without a calibration set the indicative rung applies, and every output is marked uncalibrated.

### 8.4 Obtainability test

The test starts at the indicative rung and steps down one rung at a time until all five conditions pass. That rung is the obtainable rung.

| # | Condition | Question | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | Produced | Does a record of this type exist, or could the system generate it without redesign? | D7, D8, D9, supplier documentation, interviews |
| T2 | Aggregate | Can it be given without individual decisions, {customer} data or the model? | Nature of the record |
| T3 | Reachable | Is there a route for it to reach the {entity}: a term in force, or a contracting point where one could be added? | Field 14, next renewal date |
| T4 | Checkable | Can someone independent of the party producing it verify it? | Field 20 |
| T5 | Timely | Can it arrive in time for the {entity} to act and meet its own notification obligations? | Agreement timing terms, {entity}'s incident process |

T3 records whether a term exists and what it says. Whether the term is sufficient or enforceable is a question to counsel.

**Confidence.** High where the record has been seen. Medium where the agreement or supplier documentation describes it. Low where the rung is inferred from the type of system.

### 8.5 Worked illustration

Illustrative only, not drawn from any client.

| Field | Entry |
| --- | --- |
| Arrangement | Outside claims manager under a claims agreement (B1) |
| What the AI does | Triage model routes each new motor claim to fast-track payment or investigation. No person reviews the routing |
| Authority tier | A3, decision |
| Failure consequence | C4, {customer} harm |
| Indicative rung | E3 by base rule, raised to E4 by the proposed adjustment |
| Evidence received today | E1: a due diligence response naming the triage tool |
| Obtainability | E4 fails T3 (audit clause reaches financial records only). E3 fails T1 (no trigger defined). E2 passes all five |
| Obtainable rung | E2, medium confidence |
| Question to counsel | Does the audit clause reach an aggregate record of automated triage outcomes? What can the {entity} require at renewal? |

## 9. Findings

### 9.1 Finding types

One finding is recorded per arrangement, after counsel has set the required rung. The deck names the first three outcomes. F4 is proposed here because no provider is approached.

| Code | Finding | Condition | What is recorded |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | Evidence obtainable | Obtainable rung is at or above the required rung | The evidence, who produces it, and how it is checked |
| F2 | Gap | Obtainable rung is below the required rung | The gap in rungs, which test failed, and the gap owner |
| F3 | No reasonable reach | Counsel determines the {entity} cannot reasonably require evidence at this boundary | Counsel's determination and its basis, with the technical classification beside it |
| F4 | Not determinable on documents (proposed) | The documents do not show whether AI is used, or what it can do | The specific question that would resolve it, and who could answer it |

### 9.2 Gap rating (proposed, for confirmation)

Gap size is the required rung minus the obtainable rung. Priority combines gap size with failure consequence.

| Gap size | C1 or C2 | C3 | C4 or C5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 rung | Low | Low | Medium |
| 2 rungs | Low | Medium | High |
| 3 or more rungs | Medium | High | High |

A gap at low confidence (field 22) is reported at its rated priority with the confidence shown beside it. It is not downgraded.

### 9.3 Gap owner and closing route

Each F2 names one owner. The assessment records the routes available; who closes a gap, and with what, is a separate decision for the {entity}.

| Failed test | Usual owner | Routes available |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T1, produced | The provider, or the {entity}'s AI team at B3 | The provider's own solution · a tool the {entity} already has · a boundary control and evidence design, if the {entity} asks |
| T2, aggregate | The provider | Redesign of the record so it carries aggregates and references only |
| T3, reachable | The GC, through counsel | Evidence terms at the next contracting point, with a technical schedule beside the clauses |
| T4, checkable | The {entity}'s second or third line | Appointment of an independent verifier; verification terms in the agreement |
| T5, timely | The arrangement owner | Notification timing aligned to the {entity}'s own windows |

### 9.4 Finding worksheet

One worksheet per arrangement. It is the working paper the independent reviewer checks and the source for the annex.

| Part | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| A. Identification | Arrangement ID, parties, boundary types, reason selected, worksheet version, preparer, reviewer |
| B. Chain map | Each party, what it does, where it is, and each place AI acts, with register entry IDs |
| C. Facts | Register fields 4 to 14 for each entry, each with its source reference |
| D. Classification | Authority tier and failure consequence, each with a two-line rationale tied to the facts in part C |
| E. Ladder | Indicative rung, any adjustment and reason, evidence received today |
| F. Obtainability | Result of T1 to T5 at each rung tested, the obtainable rung and confidence |
| G. Questions to counsel | Each question, date sent, response, date received |
| H. Counsel's determinations | Fields 23 to 25, transcribed with question references |
| I. Finding | Finding type, gap size and priority, failed test, gap owner, routes available, and, when calibrated, the due date and interim position (P5) |
| J. Not known | Every field recorded as not known, and what would resolve it |

### 9.5 Question-to-counsel template

| Field | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Reference | QC-01 onward |
| Arrangement and entry | ARR and REG IDs |
| Which of the seven questions | 1 to 4, or 7 |
| Facts | What the documents show, with source references. No characterisation |
| Question | One question, answerable with a determination |
| Why it matters to the assessment | Which register field and which test depend on it |
| Response | Counsel's wording, unedited |
| Status | Open · answered · open with owner |

Listed so the interfaces are clear. These are not Triodian deliverables.

### 10.3 Technical annex outline

1. Purpose, and the question the assessment answers
2. What was and was not done: no data, no provider involvement, no production access, no legal advice
3. The set, and why each arrangement was selected
4. Method: register, seven questions, ladder, obtainability test
5. Summary table of findings
6. Finding by arrangement
7. Patterns across the set: which test fails most often, and at which boundary
8. Routes available for each gap, without recommendation of any product
9. Limitations and confidence, including the not-known count
10. Appendices: register extract, question log, source index

### 10.4 Language rules for every deliverable

- State what the documents show and what the classification is. Do not state what the law requires.
- Use "indicative" for Triodian's rung and "required" only for counsel's.
- Use "gap" only where counsel has set a required rung above the obtainable one.
- Name no product, including Triodian's.
- Report aggregates and references only. No decision, {customer} detail or model content appears anywhere.
- Record the calibration status and version on every output.

## 11. Quality control

### 11.1 Review points

| # | Review | When | Reviewer | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Set review | End of phase 1 | Counsel and GC | Selection criteria applied; each boundary type represented |
| R2 | Register completeness | End of phase 2 | Delivery manager | Fields 1 to 14 complete or not known; every value sourced and dated |
| R3 | Classification review | During phase 3 | A second Triodian reviewer, not the classifier | Tier re-derived from fields 11 to 13 without sight of the original; differences resolved and logged |
| R4 | Validation | End of phase 3 | Validation (Triodian) | Rules in sections 8.3 and 8.4 applied consistently across entries; every adjustment has a reason; every obtainable rung has five test results |
| R5 | Legal-line check | Before any draft leaves Triodian | Method owner | No sentence states what the law requires; "required" and "gap" used only as section 10.4 allows |
| R6 | Counsel review | Phase 5 | Counsel | Draft seen by counsel first; determinations transcribed accurately |
| R7 | Independent check | Phase 6 | Independent reviewer | Is the assessment sound, and are its findings supported? |

### 11.2 Evidence standards

- **Traceable.** A reader can go from any finding to the test results, to the register fields, to the source document and page.
- **Reproducible.** A second classifier given the same part C facts reaches the same tier and rung. R3 tests this on every entry, since the set is small.
- **Dated.** Every source carries the date it was produced and the date it was read.
- **Verbatim where it matters.** Agreement terms and counsel's determinations are quoted, not paraphrased.
- **Disagreements kept.** Where classifier and reviewer differed, both positions and the resolution stay on the worksheet.

### 11.3 Working papers

- Marked, stored and circulated as counsel directs under the privilege position it determines.
- Versioned. Each worksheet shows preparer, reviewer and date for every version.
- No {customer}, claimant or staff personal data is collected. If a document supplied contains it, it is returned and a redacted copy requested.
- No provider confidential material is sought. Documents are supplied by the {entity} from what it already holds.
- Retained or destroyed at close as counsel directs.

### 11.4 Exceptions log

Any departure from this framework is logged with the reason and who approved it: a substituted arrangement, an interview not held, a document not supplied, a review point skipped. The log is an appendix to the annex.

### 11.5 Measures reported at close

| Measure | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Entries by boundary type and authority tier | Shows what the set covered |
| Fields not known, by arrangement | Shows how much rests on missing facts |
| Findings by type and priority | The headline result |
| Obtainable rungs by confidence level | Shows how firm the result is |
| Failed tests by type and boundary | Shows where evidence breaks down in the chain |
| Classifier and reviewer differences | Shows how repeatable the classification was |
| Questions to counsel: sent, answered, open | Shows what remains undetermined |

## 12. Assumptions, dependencies and open items

### 12.1 Assumptions

- The set is four arrangements. A larger set extends phases 2 and 3 roughly in proportion.
- The {entity} supplies documents D1 to D6 in week 1. Late documents move the plan day for day.
- Counsel answers questions to counsel within five working days.
- The {entity} has a current AI inventory. If it has none, phase 2 starts from the material service provider register and takes longer.
- The independent reviewer's check fits inside week 4. Its scope and criteria are not defined in either deck and are to be agreed with the CRO.

deliverables.name: Control-library shape for the {entity}'s own AI boundary
deliverables.contents: For B3 entries only: the categories of rule the {entity} would need to state for its own staff's use, and the record each would produce. Shape only, with no product specified
deliverables.accepted: Reviewed by the {entity}'s AI governance lead for fit with the existing framework

deliverables.name: Technical schedule, tolerance and trigger design

deliverables.accepted: Counsel confirms each item maps to a clause or to a stated reason for none

deliverables.name: Technical annex, in Triodian's name
